bugslife.guide.ladybug.habitat: Crops and farmland on sunny days. Also climbs tree trunks.
bugslife.guide.ladybug.fact: A ladybug can eat fifty aphids a day. Set a few loose on your farm: they hunt aphids and help crops grow.
bugslife.guide.aphid.habitat: On crops, and on the tops of leaves.
bugslife.guide.aphid.fact: Aphids sip plant sap and drip sweet honeydew. Many are born already carrying the next generation.
bugslife.guide.firefly.habitat: Over grass on warm nights, especially near water.
bugslife.guide.firefly.fact: Fireflies make cold light. Neighbours flash in unison, just like the synchronous fireflies of the Smoky Mountains.
bugslife.guide.cricket.habitat: Around villages at night, and now and then in plains grass.
bugslife.guide.cricket.fact: Only males chirp, by rubbing their wings together. Count the chirps in 14 seconds and add 40 to get the temperature in Fahrenheit.
bugslife.guide.pill_bug.habitat: Damp, dim places: moss, podzol, mud and shallow caves.
bugslife.guide.pill_bug.fact: Not an insect but a land crustacean, closer to a shrimp. Get too close and it rolls into an armoured ball.
bugslife.guide.water_strider.habitat: Skating on still fresh water in the daytime.
bugslife.guide.water_strider.fact: Water-repelling hairs on its legs let it stand on the surface tension of the water.
bugslife.guide.monarch.fact: Monarchs migrate thousands of miles. Watch one sip nectar and it may spread flowers across the grass nearby.
bugslife.guide.silk_moth.habitat: Among birch and dark oak leaves at dusk and after dark.
bugslife.guide.silk_moth.fact: Its cocoon is a single silk thread up to a kilometre long. Like every moth, it cannot resist a bright light.
bugslife.guide.dragonfly.habitat: Darting over rivers, lakes and swamps.
bugslife.guide.dragonfly.fact: Dragonflies catch nearly every insect they chase, and each of their four wings moves on its own.
bugslife.guide.dung_beetle.habitat: Wherever cows, sheep, pigs, goats or horses graze.
bugslife.guide.dung_beetle.fact: Dung beetles steer by the Milky Way. They follow grazing animals around and leave rich frass behind.
bugslife.guide.cave_weta.fact: Its antennae are many times its body length, for feeling through the dark. It leaps away from loud footsteps.
bugslife.guide.walking_stick.habitat: Hidden among the leaves of any tree.
bugslife.guide.walking_stick.fact: It sways like a twig in the wind and freezes the instant it is watched. A frozen stick is an easy catch.
bugslife.guide.jewel_beetle.habitat: Only on birch trunks, in the daytime.
bugslife.guide.jewel_beetle.fact: Its colour comes from microscopic layers in the shell rather than pigment. Its wing cases were once worn as jewellery.
bugslife.guide.stag_beetle.habitat: On oak and dark oak trunks after dark.
bugslife.guide.stag_beetle.fact: Those huge 'antlers' are jaws. Rival males wrestle with them, but they are too big to bite with.
bugslife.guide.glowworm.habitat: Hanging from cave ceilings, most of all in lush and dripstone caves.
bugslife.guide.glowworm.fact: Not a worm but a gnat larva. It lowers glowing, sticky silk threads to snare prey in the dark.
bugslife.guide.hercules_beetle.habitat: On jungle trunks at night, and only in jungles.
bugslife.guide.hercules_beetle.fact: One of the largest beetles in the world, and for its size one of the strongest animals alive.
bugslife.guide.ember_beetle.habitat: Scuttling over netherrack, basalt and nylium in the Nether.
bugslife.guide.ember_beetle.fact: Its shell is cracked basalt glowing with inner heat. Fire does not bother it at all.
bugslife.guide.sculk_mite.habitat: Creeping over sculk in the Deep Dark.
bugslife.guide.sculk_mite.fact: It feels every footstep. Walk normally and it burrows away; sneak, and it never knows you were there.
bugslife.guide.golden_scarab.habitat: On desert sand under the stars.
bugslife.guide.golden_scarab.fact: Ancient peoples saw the rolling sun in the scarab. This one flees any clumsy approach, so sneak up on it.
bugslife.guide.void_moth.habitat: Drifting among chorus plants and end rods in the End.
bugslife.guide.void_moth.fact: It flickers between places like an enderman. Swing and miss, and it blinks away.
bugslife.guide.worker_ant.habitat: Open dirt and grass by day, marching in columns.
bugslife.guide.worker_ant.fact: Ants follow one another in long lines. Their columns will seek out aphids to tend, and they will always follow a queen.
bugslife.guide.earwig.habitat: Dark nooks at night: under the forest canopy and around villages.
bugslife.guide.earwig.fact: Despite the legend, earwigs do not crawl into ears. They do hate light, and scuttle off to the darkest corner they can find.
bugslife.guide.termite.habitat: Savannas, and anywhere near fallen logs.
bugslife.guide.termite.fact: Termites digest wood. Drop a stick, a sapling or some planks near one and it will happily chew them into frass.
bugslife.guide.millipede.fact: Not quite a thousand legs, but plenty. Threatened, it coils into a spiral - and it oozes a toxin, so don't grab it bare-handed.
bugslife.guide.caddisfly_larva.habitat: On the beds of rivers and streams.
bugslife.guide.caddisfly_larva.fact: The larva glues pebbles and sand grains into a tube around itself with its own silk, and lives underwater inside it.
bugslife.guide.mosquito.habitat: Over swamps and still water at night.
bugslife.guide.mosquito.fact: Only the females bite. One will home in on you at night, take a sip, and fly off too full to bother you again.
bugslife.guide.mayfly.fact: Adult mayflies have no working mouths and live for mere minutes to hours. Catch one quickly - or it will be gone.
bugslife.guide.grasshopper.fact: A grasshopper can leap twenty times its own length. Walk towards one and it is off in a single enormous bound.
bugslife.guide.springtail.habitat: On snow, even in the coldest weather.
bugslife.guide.springtail.fact: Also called the snow flea. A tail spring folded under its belly flings it many times its height in an instant.
bugslife.guide.whirligig_beetle.habitat: Spinning on still ponds and slow rivers.
bugslife.guide.whirligig_beetle.fact: Its eyes are split in two: one half looks above the water, the other below. It swims in dizzy circles on the surface.
bugslife.guide.stink_bug.fact: Frighten one and it releases a cloud of foul-smelling chemicals that will turn your stomach.
bugslife.guide.orb_weaver.habitat: Beside tree trunks and fences at night.
bugslife.guide.orb_weaver.fact: It spins a fresh web at dusk. Any flying bug that blunders into it is stuck fast - and soon eaten.
bugslife.guide.tick.habitat: In the long grass and ferns of forests and taigas.
bugslife.guide.tick.fact: Ticks wait on grass stems with their front legs outstretched, ready to climb aboard any animal that brushes past.
bugslife.guide.centipede.fact: A fast, fierce predator with venomous claws. It hunts down silverfish and endermites - a welcome guest in any stronghold.
bugslife.guide.jumping_spider.habitat: Sunny walls and fences, especially in villages.
bugslife.guide.jumping_spider.fact: Its huge front eyes see in colour and follow your every move. Hold up something shiny and it may dance for you.
bugslife.guide.honeypot_ant.fact: Some workers are living larders, their bellies swollen with nectar. Offer it a glass bottle and it will share some honey.
bugslife.guide.antlion.habitat: Buried in the sand of deserts and beaches.
bugslife.guide.antlion.fact: It waits buried with only its jaws showing. Step on it and you will be grabbed and slowed while it tries to drag you under.
bugslife.guide.bookworm.habitat: Beside bookshelves: libraries, villages, strongholds and mansions.
bugslife.guide.bookworm.fact: Booklice feed on the paste and mould in old books. This one seems to be reading them. It sheds paper as it goes.
bugslife.guide.cicada.habitat: Clinging to acacia trunks in the savanna heat.
bugslife.guide.cicada.fact: The loudest insect alive. It spends years underground as a nymph and leaves its old split skin behind on the bark.
bugslife.guide.katydid.habitat: Under the forest canopy at night.
bugslife.guide.katydid.fact: Katydids answer each other's calls. Play a note block nearby and they will sing the same note back and come to find it.
bugslife.guide.hawk_moth.habitat: Flower meadows and flower forests by day.
bugslife.guide.hawk_moth.fact: Often mistaken for a hummingbird. It hovers in front of a flower on a blur of wings, sipping through its long tongue.
bugslife.guide.sakura_moth.fact: Wherever it lingers, fresh pink petals seem to drift down and gather on the grass.
bugslife.guide.paper_wasp.fact: It builds its nest from chewed wood pulp - real paper. Harm one and every wasp nearby will come after you.
bugslife.guide.locust.fact: When crowded, locusts change colour and behaviour and take to the air together in a swirling swarm.
bugslife.guide.praying_mantis.fact: The patient ambusher. It barely moves, then strikes faster than you can blink at any small bug that strays too close.
bugslife.guide.bombardier_beetle.fact: It mixes two chemicals in its abdomen and fires a boiling, popping spray at attackers. Keep your fingers clear.
bugslife.guide.diving_beetle.habitat: Underwater in ponds, lakes and swamps.
bugslife.guide.diving_beetle.fact: It carries a silvery bubble of air under its wing covers, and rows through the water with its fringed hind legs.
bugslife.guide.mole_cricket.habitat: Moist soil near water, after dark.
bugslife.guide.mole_cricket.fact: Its front legs are shovels. Come too close and it dives into the ground, only to pop up somewhere else.
bugslife.guide.darkling_beetle.habitat: Desert dunes, where it fog-basks at dawn.
bugslife.guide.darkling_beetle.fact: At dawn it stands on its head and lets fog condense on its back, then drinks the drops. Bring a bottle and it may share.
bugslife.guide.scorpion.fact: Scorpions glow under ultraviolet light - here, under the night sky. Attack one and expect a poisonous sting.
bugslife.guide.tarantula.fact: Big, hairy and surprisingly gentle. Feed one grubs and it may decide to follow you home. Sneak and use it to tell it to stay.
bugslife.guide.ice_crawler.habitat: High, frozen peaks and ice spikes.
bugslife.guide.ice_crawler.fact: It lives near freezing and dies of warmth held in a human hand. In a terrarium it needs ice beside the glass.
bugslife.guide.giant_isopod.habitat: The floor of the deep ocean.
bugslife.guide.giant_isopod.fact: A deep-sea cousin of the pill bug, as long as your forearm. It can go years without a meal, and rolls up when bothered.
bugslife.guide.luna_moth.habitat: Woodland canopies, but only under a full moon.
bugslife.guide.luna_moth.fact: Pale green, with long swallowtails that confuse bats. It is only ever seen on nights when the moon is full.
bugslife.guide.morpho.fact: Its blue is not pigment but structure: microscopic scales that bend light. Every wingbeat flashes brilliant blue.
bugslife.guide.owl_butterfly.habitat: Dark forests and jungles at dusk and night.
bugslife.guide.owl_butterfly.fact: The huge eyespots on its wings mimic an owl's stare. Phantoms keep well away from anyone near one.
bugslife.guide.leaf_insect.habitat: Jungle and bamboo leaves - good luck spotting it.
bugslife.guide.leaf_insect.fact: The master of disguise: while it keeps still it is simply invisible. Try looking through a spyglass.
bugslife.guide.click_beetle.habitat: Forest floors at night, headlights on.
bugslife.guide.click_beetle.fact: Two glowing spots on its back look like headlights. When cornered it flips into the air with a loud click.
bugslife.guide.sea_skater.habitat: Far out on the open ocean.
bugslife.guide.sea_skater.fact: The only insect that lives on the open sea, skating on the waves hundreds of miles from shore.
bugslife.guide.mushroom_beetle.fact: A pleasing fungus beetle with a mushroom of its own. Little mushrooms sprout on the mycelium wherever it wanders.
bugslife.guide.rain_beetle.fact: It spends years underground and comes up only when rain soaks the soil. When the rain stops, so does the beetle.
bugslife.guide.atlas_moth.habitat: Beside jungle leaves on the darkest nights.
bugslife.guide.atlas_moth.fact: One of the largest moths in the world, with wingtips shaped like snake heads. It has no mouth, so it can never be fed or bred.
bugslife.guide.soul_moth.habitat: Soul sand valleys in the Nether.
bugslife.guide.soul_moth.fact: Its wings burn with cold blue flame. Where other moths chase torches, this one circles soul fire and soul lanterns.
bugslife.guide.gust_moth.habitat: The tuff and copper halls of trial chambers.
bugslife.guide.gust_moth.fact: It rides the breezes of the trial chambers. Approach carelessly and a gust from its wings will blow you away.
bugslife.guide.shulker_mite.habitat: Among the purpur of End cities.
bugslife.guide.shulker_mite.fact: It lives in a shell like a tiny shulker and floats on its own levitation. Brush against it and you will float too.
bugslife.guide.chorus_weevil.fact: Too much chorus fruit, perhaps. It commutes from plant to plant by teleporting, trailing purple sparks.
bugslife.guide.echo_moth.fact: Its wings swallow sound. Near an echo moth, no vibration travels: sculk sensors stay dark and wardens hear nothing.
bugslife.guide.queen_ant.habitat: Found only where a colony of worker ants is already marching.
bugslife.guide.queen_ant.fact: Every worker follows her. With worker ants in the same terrarium she sets them to double time, and she makes royal jelly.
bugslife.guide.storm_beetle.fact: It crawls up out of hiding only in the wildest storms, and draws lightning down onto itself - unharmed, and crackling.
bugslife.guide.crystal_beetle.fact: Its shell is living crystal that slowly grows. Keep one and it will shed amethyst - and, very rarely, a diamond.
